sources.label: d042-isotopes-iaea-primary
facts: Isotopes have the same proton number and different neutron numbers.
Their chemical properties are almost the same, while their masses and physical properties differ.
Stable and radioactive isotopes are distinguished by nuclear stability, not by a different element identity.
sources.locator: Paragraph beginning Atoms with the same number of protons.
exclusions: Do not import the article generalization that the first80 elements all have stable isotopes.
Equal electron numbers require the neutral-atom comparison; nuclear charge is the element-defining quantity.
No medical use, quantitative isotope count or unrelated application is added to this lesson.

sources.label: d042-soddy-nobel-primary
facts: The speech identifies Frederick Soddy as a principal author of isotope theory and connects isotope identity to occupying the same periodic-table position.
It connects the radioactive displacement rules to nuclear charge: emitted alpha particles reduce charge by2, while emitted negative beta electrons correspond to a charge increase by1.
It distinguishes isotope identity from equal atomic weights and describes the radioactive origins of the isotope concept.

exclusions: A historical speech is not evidence that beta electrons pre-exist inside nuclei.
The speech does not independently date the source1911 hypothesis or the following Thomson experiment; no date verification is claimed.
